output.summary: KEP-614 adds SCTP as an additional protocol option beside TCP and UDP for Kubernetes Service, NetworkPolicy, and ContainerPort. The KEP reached implemented status and stable stage.
output.rationale: SCTP is widely used in telecommunications, and applications needing it could not use native Kubernetes service discovery or NetworkPolicy. The KEP adds SCTP as a protocol value so these applications can use kube-dns service discovery and native network policy control. Multi-homed SCTP and cloud load balancer support were explicitly excluded from scope.

alternatives.why_not: Non-goal: it depends on managing multiple IP addresses for a pod and NAT support for multihomed associations in SCTP-related conntrack modules.

alternatives.option: Add SCTP support to cloud provider load balancers
alternatives.why_not: Non-goal: the KEP says it does not implement SCTP into cloud-specific load balancer implementations, although Kubernetes will not restrict SCTP for type=LoadBalancer Services.

evidence.quote: enable the usage of the SCTP protocol in Kubernetes [Service], [NetworkPolicy], and [ContainerPort] as an additional protocol value option beside the current TCP and UDP options
Once SCTP support is added as a new protocol option those applications that require SCTP as L4 protocol on their interfaces can be deployed on Kubernetes clusters on a more straightforward way
It is not a goal to support multi-homed SCTP associations. Such a support also depends on the ability to manage multiple IP addresses for a pod
we do not implement the support of SCTP into the cloud specific load balancer implementations
